dialogue.origin: こんにちは。相談員です。
dialogue.content: Hello. I'm the counselor.

dialogue.origin: ご相談にきていただきありがとうございます。今日は、どのようなご相談でしょうか。
dialogue.content: Thank you for coming in for a consultation. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.origin: 学校に行きたくないんです
dialogue.content: I don't want to go to school.

dialogue.origin: 学校に行きたくないんですね、、、、。
dialogue.content: You don't want to go to school, I see...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: お話の前に、あなたの年齢と性別を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.content: Before we begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.origin: 13歳　女です
dialogue.content: I'm 13 years old, and I'm a girl.

dialogue.origin: 教えてくれてありがとうございます。中学校1年生ですね。では、お話しに戻りますが、学校に行きたくないとの事だけど、もう少し詳しく教えてもらえますか？
dialogue.content: Thank you for sharing that. So you're in the first year of junior high school. Getting back to what you said, that you don't want to go to school, could you tell me a little more about that?

dialogue.origin: 学校に行っても友達もいないし。勉強もわからなくてつまらない
dialogue.content: Even when I go to school, I don't have any friends. I don't understand the schoolwork, so it's boring.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね、、、、。それは、つまらないよね。いつ頃からそんな風に感じるのかな？
dialogue.content: I see. That must feel really boring. When did you start feeling this way?

dialogue.origin: 夏休みが終わって、9月から学校が始まってから
dialogue.content: Since summer vacation ended and school started in September.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだね、、、。じゃぁ、もう一か月もつまらない感じなんだね。
dialogue.content: I see. So you've been feeling bored for a month now.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 何かきっかけはあったんですか？
dialogue.content: Was there any particular trigger?

dialogue.origin: 女の子たちのグループに私は入れなくて、みんな楽しそうにしているけど私はいつも独りぼっち
dialogue.content: I can't get into any of the girls' groups. Everyone looks like they're having fun, but I'm always all alone.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだ、、、。周りは楽しそうなのに、自分だけ1人って思ったら、寂しいし、辛い気持ちになるよね、、、。1学期はどんな感じだったかな？
dialogue.content: I see... When you see everyone around you having fun and feel like you're the only one alone, it must feel lonely and painful. What was the first semester like?

dialogue.origin: 夏休み前は、グループに入ってない子とかが話しかけてきてくれて、少しは話せる友達がいました
dialogue.content: Before summer vacation, some other kids who weren't in groups would talk to me, and I had a few friends I could talk to.

dialogue.origin: うんうん、そうだったんだね。話しかけてくれた子たちも、今はグループになっちゃったって感じなのかな？
dialogue.content: I see, so that's how it was. And do you feel like those kids who used to talk to you have now formed their own groups?

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: それは、さびしいと思っちゃうね、、、。
dialogue.content: That must make you feel lonely...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 一番寂しいな、辛いな、と思うのはどんな時かな？
dialogue.content: When do you feel the loneliest or the most pain?

dialogue.origin: みんなの話についていけなくて、会話が続かないし私はみんなに嫌われているんじゃないかな。。って思ったときかな
dialogue.content: I guess it's when I can't keep up with everyone's conversations, the conversation doesn't continue, and I start to think that maybe everyone hates me.

dialogue.origin: そっか～。嫌われてるかもしれないと思ったら、不安になっちゃうよね、、、。それは休み時間とか、登下校の時とかかな？教室移動の時とか？
dialogue.content: I see. Thinking that you might be disliked must make you feel anxious... Does that happen during breaks, on the way to or from school, or when moving between classrooms?

dialogue.origin: 休み時間や昼休みの時です
dialogue.content: During recess and lunch breaks.

dialogue.origin: そうなだね、、、。お休み時間は楽しそうにしてる子はホントに楽しそうだもんね、、、、。寂しくなっちゃうね。
dialogue.content: I see... During breaks, the kids who are having fun look really happy, don't they? That must make you feel lonely.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 9月から段々そうなったとの事だけど、学校は毎日行っているのかな？
dialogue.content: You mentioned this has been happening gradually since September; have you been going to school every day?

dialogue.origin: はい、休みたいと思ってもお母さんは許してくれないから
dialogue.content: Yes, because even if I want to stay home, my mom won't let me.

dialogue.origin: そっかそっか、、、、。つらい想いの中、毎日通ってるんだね、、、。頑張ってるんだね、、、。
dialogue.content: I see... So you're going every day, even though it's so painful for you. You're really trying hard.

dialogue.origin: 学校に行こうとするとお腹が痛くなったり、気持ちが悪いときもあるけど、お母さんは我慢できるなら学校に行きなさいって、休ませてくらないんです
dialogue.content: When I'm about to go to school, I sometimes get a stomachache or feel sick, but my mom just says, "If you can bear it, go to school," and won't let me rest.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだね、、、、。お腹が痛くなっちゃうほどなのに、お母さんはわかってくれないんだね、、、。それはしんどいね、、、。そんな中、我慢して行ってるんだね、、、。
dialogue.content: I see... Even though it gets so bad you have a stomachache, your mom doesn't understand... That must be so tough. And you're still enduring it and going to school...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 疲れてしまうね、、、。
dialogue.content: That must be exhausting...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: そうだよね、、、。あなた（もしよければなんと呼んだら良いか教えてもらえますか？）は、どんな風になればいいなぁって思うことがありますか？
dialogue.content: I can imagine... Is there anything you wish would happen? (By the way, if you don't mind, could you tell me what I should call you?)

dialogue.origin: ニックネームでもいいですか？
dialogue.content: Is a nickname okay?

dialogue.origin: もちろんです。もしよければ教えてね。
dialogue.content: Of course. Please tell me, if you'd like.

dialogue.origin: あなたで良ければ、それでも全然大丈夫です。
dialogue.content: If you'd prefer I just say "you," that's perfectly fine as well.

dialogue.origin: ちゃこでお願いします
dialogue.content: Please call me Chako.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます！ちゃこさんと呼ばせてもらいますね。
dialogue.content: Thank you! I'll call you Chako-san, then.

dialogue.origin: は
dialogue.content: Oh.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: ちゃこさんは、この先、こんな風になったらいいなぁと思うことがありますか？
dialogue.content: Chako-san, is there a way you’d like things to be going forward?

dialogue.origin: 学校やめたいんですけど、だめですか？
dialogue.content: I want to quit school... Is that bad?

dialogue.origin: 学校やめたいんだね、、、、。ちゃこさんの状況を思うと、そう思っても当然だよね、、、、。それほどしんどいんだね、、、
dialogue.content: You want to quit school... Considering your situation, it's completely natural to feel that way. It must be that difficult for you...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: でもお母さんが怖いから、学校やめたいなんて言えないし・・
dialogue.content: But I'm scared of my mom, so I can’t tell her I want to quit school...

dialogue.origin: うんうん。お母さん怖いんだね、、、、。
dialogue.content: I see. You're scared of your mom...

dialogue.origin: お母さんは、どんな感じのお母さんなのかな？
dialogue.content: What kind of person is your mom?

dialogue.origin: いっそのこと、学校が火事で燃えたらいいのに、って思ってしまいます
dialogue.content: I sometimes wish the school would just burn down in a fire.

dialogue.origin: お母さんは普通の人だと思います
dialogue.content: I think my mom is a normal person.

dialogue.origin: 火事で燃えちゃえばいいと思うほど嫌なんだね、、、。
dialogue.content: You hate it so much that you wish it would burn down.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 明日も行きたくないです
dialogue.content: I don't want to go tomorrow, either.

dialogue.origin: うんうん、そう思うのも分かります。お母さんには、学校でのことは話したことあるかな？
dialogue.content: I understand why you feel that way. Have you ever talked to your mom about what's happening at school?

dialogue.origin: 勉強もわからないから、ずっと座っているのがつらいです
dialogue.content: I don't understand the lessons, so just sitting there the whole time is hard.

dialogue.origin: お母さんは仕事が忙しくて、夜も遅いからあまり話しません
dialogue.content: My mom is busy with work and comes home late, so we don't talk much.

dialogue.origin: お母さんとあまり話する時間もないんだね、、、。お母さんに少しでも学校でのことが分かってもらえたらちゃこさんの気持ちも変わりそうかな？
dialogue.content: So you don't have much time to talk with your mom... Do you think you'd feel differently if your mom could understand even a little about what's going on at school?

dialogue.origin: 変わるというか、楽になる、、、かな？
dialogue.content: Or rather, might it make things a bit easier?

dialogue.origin: お母さんに学校に行きたくないなんて、本当のこと言ったら怒られるから話したくないです
dialogue.content: If I tell my mom the truth, that I don't want to go to school, she'll get angry, so I don't want to talk to her about it.

dialogue.origin: 少しぐらいお腹が痛くても、休んではダメって言うくらいだから
dialogue.content: She's the type to say I can't stay home even if my stomach hurts a little.

dialogue.origin: 学校がつまらないなんて怖くて言えないです
dialogue.content: I'm too scared to say that school is boring.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。そっかそっか、、、。ちゃこさん一人で我慢してるんだね、、、、。
dialogue.content: I see... So you've been enduring this all by yourself, Chako-san...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: それはつらいよね、、、、。お話を聞かせてもらって、身近に本当に気持ちを話せる人がいれば、少しちゃこさんの気持ちもらくになるのかなぁと思っただけど、どうかな？
dialogue.content: That’s really hard... Listening to you, I wondered if having someone close by whom you can truly talk to about your feelings might help you feel a bit lighter. What do you think?

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 友達がほしいです
dialogue.content: I want friends.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。わかります。今は一人もお友達がいない感じなのかな？
dialogue.content: I understand. Do you feel like you don't have any friends at all right now?

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 部活とか、委員会とか、入ってるの？
dialogue.content: Are you in any clubs or committees?

dialogue.origin: 一日誰とも話さない日もあります
dialogue.content: There are days when I don't speak to anyone at all.

dialogue.origin: 入っていません
dialogue.content: I'm not in any.

dialogue.origin: 一日も話さないなんて、、、周りに人はたくさんいるのに悲しくなっちゃうね、、、。
dialogue.content: Not talking to anyone all day... that must be so sad, especially with so many people around you...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: どうにかお友達ができたらいいなと思ったんだけど、そのためにどんなことができそうか、一緒に考えてみるのはどうかな？
dialogue.content: I was thinking it would be great if you could make some friends. How about we think together about what we could do to make that happen?

dialogue.origin: はいお願いします
dialogue.content: Yes, please.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.content: Thank you.

dialogue.origin: 今は、部活も入っていなくて、クラスにもお友達がいない状況で、とてもつらい想いをしているんだよね。
dialogue.content: Right now, you're not in any clubs, have no friends in your class, and it's really painful for you.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: お友達がいたら、楽しくなりそうだなぁとも感じているんだよね。
dialogue.content: And you also feel that if you had friends, things would be more fun.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 学校でお友達がいたらどんなふうに付き合いたいですか？
dialogue.content: If you had friends at school, how would you want to interact with them?

dialogue.origin: いろんなことを話したいけど・・
dialogue.content: I'd like to talk about all sorts of things, but...

dialogue.origin: うんうん、いろんなこと話出来たら楽しそうですよね。
dialogue.content: Yes, it would be fun to be able to talk about many things.

dialogue.origin: どんなことを話していいか良くわからないです
dialogue.content: I don't really know what to talk about.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、、、。話に詰まってしまって話が続かない感じかな？
dialogue.content: I see... Do you feel like you get stuck and can't continue the conversation?

dialogue.origin: 夏休み前に話した友達も、私の話が意味わかんない？って顔していて・・
dialogue.content: Even the friends I talked to before summer vacation looked at me like, "What are you even talking about?"...

dialogue.origin: 面白い話もできないから
dialogue.content: Because I can't tell interesting stories,

dialogue.origin: 芸能界のことも知らないし・・みんなの話題についていけないって感じです
dialogue.content: I don't know about celebrities either... I feel like I can't keep up with what everyone's talking about.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだね、、、、。ついていけなくてどうしよう、、、て不安になってしまう感じかな？
dialogue.content: I see... and you start feeling anxious, like, "What should I do? I can't keep up."

dialogue.origin: 小学校までは家族で、ずっと中国に住んでしたから、日本のテレビみてなかったんです
dialogue.content: I lived in China with my family until elementary school, so I didn't watch Japanese TV.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、そうだったんですね。私も長い間中国にいたので、日本に帰ってきたときは軽いカルチャーショックを感じました。因みに、お父さんお母さんは日本の方ですか？
dialogue.content: I see, so that's why. I also lived in China for a long time, so I experienced a bit of culture shock when I returned to Japan. By the way, are your parents Japanese?

dialogue.origin: 日本語はあまり得意じゃなくて
dialogue.content: I'm not very good at Japanese.

dialogue.origin: お父さんは中国人でお母さんは日本人です
dialogue.content: My father is Chinese and my mother is Japanese.

dialogue.origin: そうだったんですね、、、、。文章を読んでいると、とても流暢なので、得意じゃないとは思わなかったですよ。
dialogue.content: I see... Reading your writing, you seem very fluent, so I wouldn't have thought you weren't good at it.

dialogue.origin: お母さんから日本語は習いました
dialogue.content: I learned Japanese from my mother.

dialogue.origin: お家で話をするときは日本語かな？
dialogue.content: Do you speak Japanese at home?

dialogue.origin: お母さん、とても熱心に教えてくれたんだね、ちゃこさんも頑張ったんですね。
dialogue.content: Your mother must have been a very dedicated teacher, and you must have worked hard too, Chako-san.

dialogue.origin: お母さんと話す時は日本語で話さないと怒られます
dialogue.content: When I talk to my mom, she gets angry if I don't speak Japanese.

dialogue.origin: お父さんとは中国語や日本語で話します
dialogue.content: I speak Chinese or Japanese with my dad.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、、、。お母さん怖いって言ってたもんね。教えてくれてありがとう。ちゃこさんは、どちらの言葉が話しやすいかな？
dialogue.content: I see... You did say your mom is scary. Thank you for telling me. Which language do you feel more comfortable speaking?

dialogue.origin: やっぱり中国語かな
dialogue.content: Probably Chinese, I guess.

dialogue.origin: そっか～。そんな中で日本の学校で頑張ってきたんだね。すごいね。でも、学校で何となく居場所がない感じがしてしまっているんだね、、、
dialogue.content: I see. And you've been trying so hard at a Japanese school all this time. That's amazing. But it sounds like you feel like you don't quite belong at school...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 小学校の何年生から日本に来たのかな？
dialogue.content: What grade were you in when you came to Japan?

dialogue.origin: 中学に入るからって、日本に来たので6年生の終わりごろです
dialogue.content: We came to Japan because I was starting junior high, so it was around the end of sixth grade.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだね、じゃぁ、まだ日本に来て一年もたっていないんだね。ほんとに頑張って日本語も勉強したんだね。ほんとにすごいと思うよ。そこのところは自分をほめてあげてほしいと思います。
dialogue.content: I see, so you haven't even been in Japan for a full year yet. You've really worked hard studying Japanese. I think that's truly incredible. I hope you can give yourself credit for that.

dialogue.origin: (スミマセン、１時間以上たってしまいました。私は時間は大丈夫なので続けさせていただければと思いますが、いかがいたしましょうか。）
dialogue.content: (I apologize, it's been over an hour. I'm fine on time, so I'd be happy to continue if you are, but what would you like to do?)

dialogue.origin: はいありがとうございます。
dialogue.content: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.origin: （12時までなら大丈夫です）
dialogue.content: (I'm okay until 12 o'clock.)

dialogue.origin: （ありがとうございます。では、もう少し続けさせていただきます。）お話を聞いていて、お友達がいれば楽しくなるというのはその通りだと思うんだけど
dialogue.content: (Thank you. Then let's continue a bit longer.) Listening to you, I agree that having friends would make things more enjoyable, but...

dialogue.origin: 先ずは、学校の中で自分の心地よいことを見つけてみるのはどうかなと思ったんだけど、、、、。どう思いますか？
dialogue.content: I was thinking, how about we first try to find something at school that makes you feel comfortable? What do you think about that?

dialogue.origin: よくわからないです
dialogue.content: I'm not sure what you mean.

dialogue.origin: 言葉足らずでごめんね。例えば、言葉が苦手で、困っているってことをわかってもらえそうな場所があるとか、そういう人がいそうとか、、、、。
dialogue.content: I'm sorry, I didn't explain that well. For example, maybe there's a place or a person who would understand that you're having trouble because of the language barrier...

dialogue.origin: 先生の話も良くわからないし・・勉強も英語以外はつまらないし
dialogue.content: I don't really understand what the teachers are saying... and all the subjects are boring except for English.

dialogue.origin: 数学は好きだったけど、先生が私のお母さんみたに怖くて
dialogue.content: I used to like math, but the teacher is scary like my mom.

dialogue.origin: 嫌いになってしまいました
dialogue.content: so I ended up disliking it.

dialogue.origin: お母さんみたいな先生って、一番いやだよね、口うるさくてキーキーいうみたいな感じかな？、
dialogue.content: A teacher like your mom must be the worst. Is she kind of nagging and shrill?

dialogue.origin: はい、女の先生で厳しいです
dialogue.content: Yes, she's a strict female teacher.

dialogue.origin: うんうん。想像できます。日本語での授業だもの、分からなくて当然だと思うよ。特に今はマスクもして口元も見えないし、、、。、
dialogue.content: I can imagine. It's a class in Japanese, so it's only natural that you don't understand. Especially now when everyone's wearing masks and you can't see their mouths...

dialogue.origin: 宿題を忘れてしまったことがあって、すごく怒られました
dialogue.content: I forgot my homework once, and she got really angry at me.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだ、、、、怖かったね、、、、。忘れたのは、どこが宿題かわからなかったのかな？
dialogue.content: I see... that must have been scary... Did you forget because you didn't know what the assignment was?

dialogue.origin: 先生が早口で言う時があって、どのページのところをやってくるのかわからなくて
dialogue.content: The teacher sometimes speaks really fast, and I couldn't understand which page we were supposed to do.

dialogue.origin: 友達にも聞けなくて・・
dialogue.content: And I couldn't ask any friends...

dialogue.origin: うんうん、そうだったんだね、、、、。ほんとに困っちゃったんだね。その時忘れた理由は言えたかな？
dialogue.content: I see, so that's what happened... You were really in a tough spot. Were you able to explain the reason why you forgot?

dialogue.origin: 仕方なくてやっていかなかったら、ノートを提出しないといかなかったから怒られました
dialogue.content: I couldn't help it so I didn't do it, but I had to turn in my notebook, so I got yelled at.

dialogue.origin: 先生が怖くて何も言えませんでした
dialogue.content: I was too scared of the teacher to say anything.

dialogue.origin: そっか、、、理由が言えなかったんだね、、、。悔しかったね、、、。
dialogue.content: I see... You couldn't tell her the reason... That must have been frustrating...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: ちゃこさんは、さぼっているわけではないのにね。ひどいね、、、。お話しを聞いて思ったことを少しお話ししてもいいかな？
dialogue.content: It's not as if you were slacking off. That feels unfair. May I share a few thoughts based on what I've heard?

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: ありがとう。ちゃこさんは、一生懸命やろうとしてるし、実際やっていると感じました。
dialogue.content: Thank you. I feel that you're trying very hard, and in fact, you are.

dialogue.origin: でも、言葉の問題があって、それをうまく表せなかったり、誤解されたりしてしまっているのかなと、、、、。
dialogue.content: But because of the language barrier, I think you're unable to express yourself well, and that might be causing misunderstandings...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: ちゃこさんの身近に、そのことをわかってくれてる人がいた方がいいと思いました。困ったと、何か話したくなった時に話せるような、、、、。
dialogue.content: I think it would be good for you to have someone close by who understands your situation. Someone you can talk to when you're in trouble or feel like you want to talk...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 出来れば、学校の中でそのような人がいると一番いいかと思うんだけど、この事を担任の先生などに話したことはあるかな？
dialogue.content: Ideally, having someone like that at school would be best. Have you ever talked about this with your homeroom teacher?

dialogue.origin: ないです
dialogue.content: No, I haven't.

dialogue.origin: そっか、、、。先生方は「日本語苦手だから仕方ないよね、、、、」と思っているかもしれないけど、まさか、ちゃこさんがこんなに大きく悩んでいるとは思っていないかもしれません。
dialogue.content: I see... The teachers might be thinking, "Well, her Japanese isn't great, so it can't be helped," but they probably have no idea how much this is truly troubling you.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Right.

dialogue.origin: なので、もし、話せそうなら担任の先生に、何を困っているかを話してみるのは1つの方法だと思ったんだけど、どうかな？
dialogue.content: So, if you feel you can, I thought one option would be to try talking to your homeroom teacher about what you're struggling with. What do you think?

dialogue.origin: 先生に話したら、先生はお母さんにも話したりしますか？
dialogue.content: If I tell my teacher, will the teacher talk to my mom?

dialogue.origin: お母さんに私が学校に行きたくないし辞めたいと思っていることが、わかってしまったら・・と思うと怖くて
dialogue.content: I'm scared to think of what would happen if my mom found out that I don't want to go to school and want to quit...

dialogue.origin: そこが心配なんだね。お母さんには黙っていて欲しいと言えば、お母さんには言わないと思うよ。そこもちゃんと先生に伝えれば大丈夫。
dialogue.content: That's what you're worried about. If you ask the teacher to keep it from your mom, I believe they won't tell her. As long as you communicate that clearly to the teacher, it should be fine.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですか？
dialogue.content: Really?

dialogue.origin: 先生って案外頼りになるよ。ちゃこさんが真剣に伝えれば、分かってくれます。
dialogue.content: Teachers can be surprisingly reliable. If you explain your situation seriously, they will understand.

dialogue.origin: 先生がお母さんに絶対に言わないなら、相談してもいいかな
dialogue.content: If the teacher absolutely won't tell my mom, then maybe I can talk to them.

dialogue.origin: でも担任の先生は、ちょっと話にくそうで勇気がいります
dialogue.content: But my homeroom teacher seems a bit hard to talk to, and it would take courage.

dialogue.origin: あんまりすきじゃないし
dialogue.content: And I don't really like them, either.

dialogue.origin: そうなんだね。それは、それでいいと思うよ。担任じゃなくても、保健室の先生とか、、、。ちゃこさんの学校には相談室痛いのはあるのかな？　そこの先生でもいいと思うよ。ちゃこさんが話やすい、わかってくれそう、と思う人に話てみてはどうかな？
dialogue.content: I see. That's perfectly fine. It doesn't have to be your homeroom teacher; it could be the school nurse. Does your school have a counseling office? The teacher there would be a good option too. How about talking to someone you feel comfortable with and who seems like they would understand?

dialogue.origin: 痛い→みたい　　間違いです、、、ごめんね。
dialogue.content: Oops, "painful" was a typo for "like." Sorry about that.

dialogue.origin: はい保健室の先生は優しそうだし、腹痛でお世話になったこともあるし
dialogue.content: Yes, the school nurse seems kind, and she's taken care of me before when I had a stomachache.

dialogue.origin: 大丈夫です
dialogue.content: It's okay.

dialogue.origin: 今度話してみようかな・・
dialogue.content: Maybe I'll try talking to her next time...

dialogue.origin: うんうん。話すことできっと、良い方向に向かっていくと思います。
dialogue.content: Yes, I think talking to her will definitely help things move in a better direction.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: なにより、ちゃこさんが少し楽になるんじゃないかな。
dialogue.content: Most importantly, I think you'll feel a little more at ease, Chako-san.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございました
dialogue.content: Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: こちらこそ、お話ししてくれてありがとう。
dialogue.content: No, thank you for talking with me.

dialogue.origin: 今日の相談はこれで大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.content: Is that all right for today’s session?

dialogue.origin: はい、大丈夫です
dialogue.content: Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.origin: ちゃこさんは、頑張ってるよ！自信を持ってね！それでは、今日の相談終わりにします。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: You're doing a great job, Chako-san! Be confident! With that, we'll end today's session. Thank you.

dialogue.origin: はい。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Yes. Thank you very much.
